data.gender_notes: Phoebe is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Phoebe, a deaconess in the church at Cenchrea, is mentioned in the New Testament as a patron and helper of Paul. Her name, which means 'lovely' or 'radiant', conveys a sense of warmth and kindness. The name Phoebe carries the meaning “Lovable, radiant maiden” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Phoebe usually hope their child will grow to embody lovable, radiant maiden and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Phoebe symbolizes the love and support that can be found in the church, and her name encourages us to nurture and care for one another.
data.etymology: Phoebe belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lovable, radiant maiden.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Phoebe total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: פיבי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פיבי נגזר מהמילה היוונית פῠ́βη (phoíbē), שפירושה זוהרית או מלכה של הירח. השם קשור למילה היוונית פῠ́bos (phoîbos), שפירושה בהיר או זוהר. בפנייה הנוצרית, השם פיבי מזוהה עם דמותה של פיבי, דיאקונת של הכנסייה הקורינתית, הנזכרת בספר הרומיים 16:1-2.

in_greek.name: Φοίβη
in_greek.long_meaning: Φοίβη (Phoíbē) σημαίνει Φωτεινή ή Λαμπρή, δηλαδή φωτεινή ή λαμπρή. Το όνομα συνδέεται με το ελληνικό ρήμα φοíbēmi, που σημαίνει να λάμπω ή να φωτίζω. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, η Φοίβη αναφέρεται ως διάκονος της εκκλησίας της Κορίνθου (Ρωμ. 16:1-2).

in_latin.name: Phoebe
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Phoebe is derived from the Greek name Φοίβη (Phoíbē), meaning bright or radiant. In Christian tradition, Phoebe is recognized as a deaconess of the Corinthian church, mentioned in Romans 16:1-2. The name has been adopted into Latin and has been used in various forms throughout Christian history.

in_english.name: Phoebe
in_english.long_meaning: The name Phoebe originates from the Greek name Φοίβη (Phoíbē), meaning bright, shining, or radiant. It is associated with the Greek word for 'bright' or 'shining', and has been used in Christian tradition since the early church. Phoebe is mentioned in the New Testament as a deaconess of the Corinthian church (Romans 16:1-2). The name has been popularized in various cultures and is often associated with qualities of light, hope, and spiritual guidance.

data.cultural_impact: Phoebe is an ancient Greek name, meaning 'shining bright' or 'bright one'. In Greek mythology, Phoebe was the mother of Apollo and the goddess of fertility and harmony. Later, in Christianity, Phoebe came to be known as a prominent deaconess and patron of the early Christian community. This cultural background has contributed to the name Phoebe's association with strength, leadership, and spiritual guidance.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Phoebe holds deep spiritual significance as it reminds us of the early Christian deaconess who personified selflessness, compassion, and dedication. Phoebe's name symbolizes the inner light that guides us on our spiritual journey. It also serves as an inspiration for individuals who embody the qualities of resilience, grace, and strength in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Phoebe, meaning "bright, radiant one," embodies the spiritual light and purity within every Christian. She is a beacon of hope, illuminating the path for others with her unwavering faith and love. In the New Testament, Phoebe is recognized as a deaconess and a servant of the church, inspiring us to serve and uplift our communities with grace and humility.
